title: 第19章 印刷符业第20章 仙籍暗流
content_zh:
吴燃灯望着案上叠放的符纸，每张“正气歌”的字迹都分毫不差，横平竖直如刀切，虽凝着正气，却少了些手写时的灵动变化。
他指尖划过纸面，眉头微蹙。
这般字迹齐整，明眼人一看便知是批量印出的，若流传开，难免引人窥破雕版之秘。
“符文如字，字见笔意，笔意藏魂。”他翻出先前手写的符章。
对比之下，手写的“正”字捺脚略重，带三分沉凝，“气”字弯钩微颤，藏一丝灵动，各有不同。
当下不再犹豫，取来十二块金桐木，每块都换了笔法。
或学颜体的浑厚，笔锋如椎，刻出的字力透木背。
或仿柳体的清劲，撇如刀削，捺似剑挑。
更有学章草的婉转，笔画连属，如流泉绕石。
刻到第七块时，他特意抖了抖手腕，让几个字带些微不可察的歪斜，恰似人手写时偶有的滞涩。
十二块雕版成时，依次印刷，符纸上的字迹果然神态各异。
有端方如古碑，有飘逸若惊鸿，便是同个“气”字，在不同雕版下，有的如劲松拔节，有的似云气舒卷。
吴燃灯将印好的符纸混在一起，便是他自己也需细辨，方能认出是哪块雕版所出。
他抚过雕版上深浅不一的刻痕，轻笑一声：“这般藏了笔意，纵是行家来看，也只当是出自同一人之手的不同符章罢了。”
窗外风过，吹得案上符纸轻响，倒像是在应和这藏巧于拙的心思。
吴燃灯将那三十张混在手写符章中的印刷符章仔细分装，外层裹了防潮的油纸，再装入刻着云纹的木盒。
随后他去了灵宝阁，快去快回，面对掌柜诧异，只说是“近日闲时所制，望掌柜过目”。
灵宝阁掌脸上笑容愈发，手里捧着那木盒，见了吴燃灯便拱手：“沈道友，您这符章当真是妙！笔力稳健，灵气纯粹，尤其是这五章‘天地人三才章’，虽然相比之前，灵气有缺失，但细看却仍是各有韵味，阁中长老看了都必然赞不绝口。”
说罢，他递过一枚暗金色的令牌，上面刻着“贵宾”二字：“阁主说了，从今往后，您便是我灵宝阁的贵宾。这是您的份例——”身后的侍从搬来三个木箱，打开一看，里面是晶莹的灵石、成册的古籍，还有炼制丹药的珍稀药材，光芒流转，灵气逼人。
“这些……”吴燃灯故作惊讶，眼底却藏着一丝了然，对方果然没有看出符章印刷的奥妙。

符章价值如初，更重要的是，他这小心藏拙所换来的安稳。
符章源源不绝，资源换取不尽，唯有这小心谨慎换来的久安才是长远之计。
《易数》有云，君子藏器于身，待时而动，何不利之有？
莫过于如此。
此时掌柜笑道：“先生放心，您的符章我们会妥善收存，只供内阁修士兑换。往后您有符章要出，只需遣人知会一声，我等亲自来取便是。”
吴燃灯点头，手上翻出一个储物袋，这也是这次的收获之一。
他走到窗边，望着天边渐沉的暮色，心中清明。
这印刷符业，是他在修仙路上找到的一条捷径，却也如同一把双刃剑，需时时握紧，步步小心。
content_en:
Wu Randeng looked at the talisman papers stacked on the table. The handwriting on each piece of "Song of Righteousness" was exactly the same. The horizontal and vertical lines were as straight as a knife. Although they were condensed with righteousness, they lacked some of the flexible changes in handwriting.
He traced his fingertips across the paper and frowned slightly.
With such neat handwriting, anyone with a discerning eye would know at a glance that it was printed in batches. If it spread, it would inevitably lead people to peek into the secret of the engraving.
"Rules are like words, the words reflect the meaning of the pen, and the meaning of the pen hides the soul." He pulled out the previously handwritten talisman.
In contrast, the handwritten word "正" is a little heavier, with a hint of concentration, while the word "Qi" has a slightly curved hook, hiding a hint of agility. Each one is different.
Without hesitation, he took twelve pieces of golden paulownia wood and changed the writing method on each piece.
Or learn the richness of Yan's body, the sharpness of his pen is as sharp as vertebrae, and the power of the carved words can penetrate the wooden back.
Or it imitates the freshness of willow body, which is like cutting with a knife and holding back like the pick of a sword.
There is also the euphemism of learning Zhangcao, and the strokes are connected together, like a flowing spring surrounding a stone.
When he reached the seventh block, he deliberately shook his wrist to make the words slightly skewed, just like the occasional hesitation in handwriting.
When the twelve engravings were completed, they were printed one after another, and the handwriting on the talisman paper had different expressions.
Some are as square as an ancient stele, and some are as graceful as a giant dragon. It is the same word "qi". Under different carvings, some are like the joints of strong pine trees, and some are like the rolling clouds.
Wu Randeng mixed the printed talisman papers together, and even he had to distinguish them carefully to identify which engraving block they came from.
He stroked the carvings with different depths and chuckled: "It hides the meaning of the brushwork. Even if it is viewed by an expert, it will just be regarded as different talismans by the same person."
The wind blowing outside the window made the talisman on the table ring softly, which seemed to be in response to this thought of hiding cleverness and clumsiness.
Wu Randeng carefully packed the thirty printed talismans mixed with the handwritten talismans, wrapped them in moisture-proof oil paper, and then put them into wooden boxes engraved with cloud patterns.
Then he went to Lingbao Pavilion and hurried back. When faced with the surprise of the shopkeeper, he only said, "I made it in my spare time recently. I hope the shopkeeper will take a look at it."
The smile on the face of the master of Lingbao Pavilion grew stronger. He held the wooden box in his hand and handed it over when he saw Wu Randeng: "Friend Daoist Shen, your talisman is really wonderful! The writing is steady and the aura is pure, especially these five chapters of the 'Three Talents of Heaven, Earth and Man'. Although the aura is lacking compared to before, they still have their own charm if you look closely. The elders in the pavilion will be full of praise after reading it."
After saying that, he handed over a dark gold token with the word "VIP" engraved on it: "The Pavilion Master said that from now on, you will be the VIP of my Lingbao Pavilion. This is your case -" The attendant behind him moved three wooden boxes and opened them. Inside were crystal clear spiritual stones, volumes of ancient books, and rare medicinal materials for refining elixirs. The light was flowing and the aura was compelling.
"These..." Wu Randeng pretended to be surprised, but there was a hint of understanding in his eyes. As expected, the other party did not see the mystery of the talisman printing.
The value of the talisman is still the same as before, and more importantly, the stability he gained from his careful hiding.
There is an endless supply of talismans and endless exchange of resources. Only the long-term peace gained by being cautious is the long-term solution.
There is a saying in "Book of Changes" that a gentleman hides his weapons in his body and waits for the time to move. What is the disadvantage?
Nothing more than that.
At this time, the shopkeeper smiled and said: "Sir, don't worry, we will store your talisman properly and only exchange it for the cabinet monks. If you want to issue a talisman in the future, just send someone to inform you, and we will come and pick it up in person."
Wu Randeng nodded and took out a storage bag, which was also one of the gains this time.
He walked to the window and looked at the sinking dusk in the sky, feeling clear in his heart.
This printing talisman industry is a shortcut he found on the road to immortality, but it is also like a double-edged sword, which needs to be held tightly at all times and be careful every step of the way.
